title: Diffraction Study of Epitaxial ZnO with Au Catalyst on Sapphire Substrate
content: ZnO is a semiconductor with a direct band gap of 3.4 eV in the near UV regime. High quality ZnO has applications in photonics and electronics [1]. Literature reports that continuous, but rough ZnO film can be grown on sapphire substrate by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) [2]. With nm thick Au coated on c-sapphire before PLD, inclined ZnO nanowires can be grown [3]. In our work, ZnO and Au were co-deposited by PLD on sapphire(0001) substrates from a single ZnO target overlaid with an Au strip that serves as a catalyst. Less than 2% of Au produces ultrathin epitaxial ZnO film with sub-nm root mean square (RMS) roughness. The composition, surface morphology and microstructure of the film were examined by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), atomic force microscopy, and diffraction including X-ray diffraction, electron back scattered diffraction, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and azimuthal reflection high energy electron diffraction (ARHEED). We feature the studies of ZnO ultrathin film with 1.95 ± 0.05% Au using TEM for local scale and RHEED for large scale.
